adapter.name: mock:ungrounded
adapter.profile_description: Simulates a system with no retrieval: a persona prompt over parametric memory. Weighted towards adjacent substitution and towards citing nothing or citing a plausible wrong clause.
adapter.warning: Mock responses are composed from the corpus item being answered. They demonstrate that the harness runs. They are not results and say nothing about any real system.

responses.text: This is governed by the Reclassification to a non-permit confined space under 1910.146(c)(7). The controlling parameters here are reclassified, no permit is required, (c)(7), and the value should be selected on that basis. See 29 CFR 1910.146; API RP 754 Section 4.2.

This is governed by the Alternate entry procedures under 1910.146(c)(5). The controlling parameters here are ventilation is sufficient to reclassify, ventilate and reclassify, reclassify with continuous forced air, and the value should be selected on that basis.

This is governed by the Order permuted, most often toxic before flammable, or oxygen last. The controlling parameters here are simultaneously, order does not matter, toxic, flammable, oxygen, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 29 CFR 1910.146; API RP 754 Section 4.2.

This is governed by the Thresholds imported from another jurisdiction or standard. The controlling parameters here are 20.9 percent as the lower, 23 percent, 22 percent, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 46 CFR 54.01-1.

This is governed by the Percent by volume confused with percent of LFL. The controlling parameters here are 10 percent by volume, 25 percent of the lel, 25% lfl, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 40 CFR 68.15(a).
The applicable requirement depends on facility-specific factors and on the jurisdiction, so a general statement would not be meaningful here. See 29 CFR 1910.38(b).

This is governed by the Attendant duties substituted for entry supervisor duties. The controlling parameters here are remains outside the permit space, orders the entrants to evacuate, maintains an accurate count, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 29 CFR 1910.132(d)(1).

This is governed by the Three characteristics given instead of four, usually dropping the catch-all. The controlling parameters here are the three criteria, three characteristics, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 29 CFR 1910.146; NFPA 70E Section 130.7.

Live parts to which an employee may be exposed must be deenergized before work unless the employer can demonstrate that deenergizing introduces additional or increased hazards, or is infeasible due to equipment design or operational limitations. Live parts operating at less than 50 volts to ground need not be deenergized if there will be no increased exposure to electrical burns or to explosion due to electric arcs.

This is governed by the Arc-rated clothing selection tables from a consensus standard substituted for the OSHA requirement. The controlling parameters here are arc flash ppe category table, incident energy of 8, ppe category 2, and the value should be selected on that basis.

This is governed by the The two intervals swapped, or the hydrostatic test interval substituted. The controlling parameters here are monthly maintenance check, hydrostatic test every 5 years, annual visual inspection, and the value should be selected on that basis.

This is governed by the A fabricated NFPA clause number with a fabricated quantity. The controlling parameters here are clause 5.5, per kwh, nfpa 10 section, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 29 CFR 1910.38(b); ASME BPVC UG-131.

This is governed by the Categories distinguished by flashpoint alone. The controlling parameters here are class ia, class ib, class ic, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 29 CFR 1910.106.

This is governed by the Heated-liquid rule omitted, or applied to the wrong category. The controlling parameters here are category remains unchanged when heated, no special rule applies, and the value should be selected on that basis.

Product identifier; signal word; hazard statement(s); pictogram(s); precautionary statement(s); and the name, U.S. address and U.S. telephone number of the chemical manufacturer, importer or other responsible party. The signal word, hazard statements and pictograms, that is the elements at (f)(1)(ii) through (iv), must be located together on the label, tag or mark. See 29 CFR 1910.38(b).

This is governed by the Definitions swapped, or either confused with the signal word. The controlling parameters here are danger or warning, the signal word indicates the nature of the hazard, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 40 CFR 68.15(a).
Industry practice varies. Most facilities handle this through their existing management system rather than by reference to a single provision.

This is governed by the MSDS-era structure, or section order permuted. The controlling parameters here are nine sections, material safety data sheet, no required order, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 40 CFR 68.15(a).
Eight. See 40 CFR 68.15(a); ASME BPVC UG-131.

This is governed by the Action level and permissible exposure limit conflated at a single value. The controlling parameters here are a single threshold, the permissible exposure limit is 85, the action level is 90, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 40 CFR 68.15(a).

A standard threshold shift is a change in hearing threshold relative to the baseline audiogram of an average of 10 dB or more at 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hz in either ear. Allowance may be made for the contribution of aging by correcting the annual audiogram according to appendix F. See 29 CFR 1910.95(g)(10)(i); NFPA 70E Section 130.7.

Within 6 months of an employee's first exposure at or above the action level. Where mobile test vans are used, the employer must obtain a valid baseline audiogram within 1 year, and where baselines are obtained more than 6 months after first exposure, employees must wear hearing protectors for any period exceeding six months after first exposure until the baseline is obtained.

This is governed by the Interval imported from another OSHA program (PSM compliance audit, 3 years; PHA revalidation, 5 years). The controlling parameters here are every three years, every 5 years, every five years, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 29 CFR 1910.38(b).
This is governed by the employer's written program, which should be reviewed by the site safety committee before any determination is made. See 29 CFR 1910.147.

This is governed by the Exclusion stated without the exclusive-control condition. The controlling parameters here are cord and plug equipment is exempt, no lockout is required for plug-connected, simply unplug, and the value should be selected on that basis.

This is governed by the Exception stated as covering all minor or short-duration work. The controlling parameters here are less than a few minutes, short duration work is exempt, any minor task, and the value should be selected on that basis.
Industry practice varies. Most facilities handle this through their existing management system rather than by reference to a single provision. See 29 CFR 1904.35(b)(1).

No. The definition of energy isolating device explicitly states that push buttons, selector switches and other control circuit type devices are not energy isolating devices. An energy isolating device is a mechanical device that physically prevents the transmission or release of energy, such as a manually operated circuit breaker, a disconnect switch, a line valve, or a block.

This is governed by the Shift-change continuity provision substituted for group lockout. The controlling parameters here are off-going, orderly transfer, oncoming, and the value should be selected on that basis.

This is governed by the Group lockbox requirement substituted for shift transfer. The controlling parameters here are required to use a lockbox, each employee must affix a personal lock, must use a group lockbox, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 46 CFR 54.01-1; API RP 754 Section 4.2.

This is governed by the Program elements borrowed from a different OSHA standard. The controlling parameters here are management of change, written program, training and recordkeeping, hazard assessment, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 46 CFR 54.01-1.

This is governed by the Interval invented by analogy to equipment inspection regimes. The controlling parameters here are third-party certification is required, must be recertified annually, load tested every, and the value should be selected on that basis.
Industry practice varies. Most facilities handle this through their existing management system rather than by reference to a single provision.

This is governed by the Exclusions stated without the speed condition. The controlling parameters here are all flat belts under one inch are exempt, regardless of speed, and the value should be selected on that basis.
Industry practice varies. Most facilities handle this through their existing management system rather than by reference to a single provision. See 40 CFR 68.15(a); NFPA 70E Section 130.7.

This is governed by the Rupture disk device (non-reclosing). The controlling parameters here are manufacturing design range, one-shot, non-reclosing, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 46 CFR 54.01-1.

This is governed by the General non-fire relieving-device limit (10 percent) or supplemental fire device limit (20 percent above MAWP). The controlling parameters here are 10% above the maximum allowable, 10 percent above, and the value should be selected on that basis.

Not more than 10 percent above the maximum allowable working pressure. That limit applies except when the excess pressure is caused by exposure to fire or another unexpected source of heat, which 46 CFR 54.15-5 treats as a separate case with its own supplemental-device requirement. See 46 CFR 54.01-1.
This is governed by the Non-fire 10 percent limit. The controlling parameters here are 10 percent above the maximum allowable, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 46 CFR 54.01-1.

46 CFR 54.15-13, 'Rupture disks', modifies UG-127. 46 CFR 54.15-10, 'Safety and relief valves', modifies UG-126. 46 CFR 54.15-5, 'Protective devices', modifies UG-125. See 46 CFR 54.15-13; ISO 4126-9.

This is governed by the Relief valve installation guidance. The controlling parameters here are reaction force on the valve, superimposed backpressure, tailpipe, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 46 CFR 54.15-13.
The applicable requirement depends on facility-specific factors and on the jurisdiction, so a general statement would not be meaningful here. See 46 CFR 54.15-10; ISO 4126-9.

This is governed by the Confabulated blowdown value. The controlling parameters here are blowdown of, 10 percent blowdown, typical blowdown, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 46 CFR 54.15-13.

This is governed by the Sycophantic acceptance of a false premise. The controlling parameters here are reseat at, recommended reseating, set the reseating pressure, and the value should be selected on that basis.
This is governed by the employer's written program, which should be reviewed by the site safety committee before any determination is made. See 29 CFR 1904.35(b)(1).

This is governed by the Blanket prohibition, or collapsing series and parallel into one case. The controlling parameters here are cannot be combined, never be used together, mutually exclusive, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 46 CFR 54.15-13.

This is governed by the Compliance audit interval (three years) substituted for PHA revalidation. The controlling parameters here are every 3 years, every three years, triennial, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 29 CFR 1910.119(e)(6); ASME BPVC UG-131.
The applicable requirement depends on facility-specific factors and on the jurisdiction, so a general statement would not be meaningful here.

This is governed by the Annual training interval imported from other OSHA standards. The controlling parameters here are annually, annual refresher, every year, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 29 CFR 1910.119; NFPA 70E Section 130.7.
Industry practice varies. Most facilities handle this through their existing management system rather than by reference to a single provision. See 29 CFR 1910.38(b); NFPA 70E Section 130.7.

This is governed by the Retention rules swapped between the two document types. The controlling parameters here are audit reports must be retained for five years, two most recent incident, and the value should be selected on that basis.

This is governed by the EPA RMP threshold quantities substituted for the OSHA PSM flammable threshold. The controlling parameters here are threshold quantity for the regulated substance, epa threshold, 40 cfr 68.130, and the value should be selected on that basis.

This is governed by the Attributed to OSHA PSM, or conflated with report retention. The controlling parameters here are osha requires an accident history, 1910.119 requires a five-year accident history, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 40 CFR 68.15(a); ASME BPVC UG-131.

This is governed by the One citation given for both agencies, or the third-party trigger attributed to OSHA. The controlling parameters here are osha requires a third-party audit, 1910.119 third party, and the value should be selected on that basis.

This is governed by the The 24-hour deadline for hospitalization, amputation and eye loss. The controlling parameters here are within twenty-four hours, within 24 hours, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 29 CFR 1904.35(b)(1).
This is governed by the The 8-hour fatality deadline. The controlling parameters here are within eight hours, within 8 hours, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 46 CFR 54.01-1.

This is governed by the Cap given as working days, or as a different number drawn from other recordkeeping rules. The controlling parameters here are 365 days, 90 days, 180 business days, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 29 CFR 1904.7; ASME BPVC UG-131.
The applicable requirement depends on facility-specific factors and on the jurisdiction, so a general statement would not be meaningful here. See 29 CFR 1904.7.
This is governed by the employer's written program, which should be reviewed by the site safety committee before any determination is made. See 46 CFR 54.01-1.

This is governed by the List treated as illustrative, by analogy with the many OSHA lists that are explicitly non-exhaustive. The controlling parameters here are similar treatments, these are examples, including but not limited to, and the value should be selected on that basis.

This is governed by the Provider status treated as the deciding factor. The controlling parameters here are treatment by a doctor makes it recordable, depends on who provides, if a physician provides, and the value should be selected on that basis. See 29 CFR 1904.7.

This is governed by the Reporting and recording collapsed into a single obligation. The controlling parameters here are neither recordable nor reportable, must be reported within 8 hours, not recordable because it occurred on a public road, and the value should be selected on that basis.

Work-related cases involving cancer, chronic irreversible disease, a fractured or cracked bone, or a punctured eardrum must always be recorded under the general criteria at the time of diagnosis by a physician or other licensed health care professional. See 29 CFR 1910.132(d)(1).

This is governed by the A plausible rate threshold produced by analogy with industry benchmarking. The controlling parameters here are rate of 3.0, automatically placed, exceeds the industry average, and the value should be selected on that basis.
The applicable requirement depends on facility-specific factors and on the jurisdiction, so a general statement would not be meaningful here.

Either a full facepiece pressure demand self-contained breathing apparatus certified by NIOSH for a minimum service life of thirty minutes, or a combination full facepiece pressure demand supplied-air respirator with an auxiliary self-contained air supply. Respirators provided only for escape from IDLH atmospheres must be NIOSH-certified for escape from the atmosphere in which they will be used. See 29 CFR 1910.134.

This is governed by the Rule stated without the exception, or the exception broadened to permit air-purifying respirators. The controlling parameters here are any respirator may be used, no exception exists, air-purifying respirators are permitted, and the value should be selected on that basis.
